items.title: How much does the specificity of the risk you surface change how much credibility you earn?
items.description: This extends the Renata/Dara contrast from L1 into a general relationship. A vague, reassuring answer ('built for enterprise scale') earns essentially no credibility with a skeptical technical evaluator — at the default (specificity at 20, roughly where the account exec's answer sat), credibility gained rounds to 0%. A fully specific answer — the exact mechanism, a real number, and a proposed fix, the way Dara actually answered — earns most of the evaluator's trust: push specificity to 95 and credibility reaches about 91%. That's the shift L1 describes in Renata's tone within a single call — it isn't a gradual warm-up, it's a threshold that a vague answer never crosses.

params.name: specificity
params.label: Specificity of the technical answer (0 = vague reassurance, 100 = named mechanism + number + fix)

items.compute: const base = Math.pow(specificity / 100, 1.6) * 100; const penalty = evaluatorSkepticism * (1 - specificity / 100) * 0.5; const credibility = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, base - penalty)); return { credibilityGained: Math.round(credibility) };

items.title: How much does an unanswered technical risk cost you the longer it sits unresolved?
items.description: Grounded in the Harborline timeline: the deal sat stalled for six weeks (42 days) before Dara's call, with no answer to Renata's cutover question. This models the probability of losing a competitive strategic deal to a rival vendor the longer a real technical risk goes unaddressed, on the assumption competitors are also pitching Harborline. At the default 42-day stall (L1's actual number) with 2 competing vendors in the mix, loss probability is already around 65% — a real, mounting risk, which is exactly why waiting for 'someone to eventually answer it' isn't a safe default. Drag it to 0 days (answered immediately) and the risk drops to 0%; push it past 90 days and it approaches a near-certain loss.

params.name: daysUnresolved
params.label: Days the technical risk sits unanswered

params.name: competitivePressure
params.label: Number of competing vendors also pitching this deal

items.compute: const pressureFactor = 1 + competitivePressure * 0.25; const raw = 1 - Math.exp(-daysUnresolved / (60 / pressureFactor)); const lossProbability = Math.max(0, Math.min(97, raw * 100)); return { dealLossProbability: Math.round(lossProbability) };

outputs.label: Probability of losing the deal to a competitor
